round: restricted-view bases: weak but structurally different
methodological_correction: Every experiment I ran today chased a STRONGER base (better backbone, more anchors, greater width, fresher anchors). Today's measurement proves that is the wrong objective: the base-to-ensemble transfer coefficient is 0.21%, and a base carrying a genuine 0.002-0.004 standalone gain contributed -0.0000013. A ridge pays only for the component of a base ORTHOGONAL to the existing span. FINDINGS 2.4 already said this: tcn45 is garbage standalone at 1.754 yet takes weight 0.07, while tcn270 at corr 0.9956 contributes zero.
why_the_pool_is_saturated: All 29 bases see the SAME thing: the full 409-day history across all channels. Collinearity above 0.99 is structurally forced. No base built on the full view can be decorrelated from the others, however good it is.
hypothesis: Deliberately RESTRICTING what a model can see produces a weak model whose errors are decorrelated from the full-view pool, which is what the ridge actually pays for.

cells.rv_intent: funnel intent only: to_cart, to_ord, search_to_cart, search_to_ord, cat_to_cart, cat_to_ord

expected_standalone: All of these should be WEAK, plausibly 1.68-1.80. A weak standalone score is NOT a failure in this round and must not be used to reject a cell.

honest_prior: This is the first round today whose design matches what the measurement says the ridge pays for, rather than contradicting it. That is a real reason for hope. It is still an untested hypothesis, and eight axes have closed negatively today.
